scope: Power-mean inequality theorem for quadrupole shape invariants and artificial rigidity artifact

theorem.statement: For any state with non-zero quadrupole deformation amplitude fluctuations (sigma_Q > 0), the third moment <Q^3> strictly exceeds <Q^2>^(3/2) by the power-mean inequality.
theorem.consequence: Defining cos(3delta) = <Q^3 cos 3delta> / <Q^2>^(3/2) mathematically forces cos(3delta) > 1.0 when delta is rigid (delta=0), producing an unphysical negative variance Var(cos 3delta) < 0.
theorem.code_truncation_artifact: Standard codes (such as GOSIA sigma.f lines 185-186) truncate negative variance to zero via IF(V.LT.0.) V=0., outputting sqrt(var) = 0.0000 deg and falsely certifying amplitude-fluctuating nuclei as angularly rigid.

checks.name: Discrete fluctuating model: GOSIA FINT cos(3delta) > 1.0
All Gaussian cases have negative variance Var(cos 3delta) < 0.0
Gaussian 10% width gives cos(3delta) ~ 1.0147 and var ~ -0.0297

conclusion: Zero angular dispersion from invariant analysis cannot prove rigid triaxiality; it can be entirely an artifact of amplitude fluctuations combined with power-mean denominator underestimation and negative variance truncation.
